curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.strand: 3.3 Language use 3.3.1 Verb ‘to have’ – present form
curriculum.outcomeText: use the present form of the verb ‘to have’ (have, has) and the objective pronouns (me, her/him, it) in varied contexts

mission.title: Have, Has, Me, Her, Him and It

interactions.prompt: At break time in a Kisumu school, I ___ a ball.
interactions.feedback: Correct! We say, ‘I have a ball.’

interactions.prompt: Musa has a book. Musa reads ___. Choose the word that replaces ‘the book’.
interactions.retryHint: A book is a thing, not a person.

interactions.prompt: At a family reading circle, match each beginning to its ending.
interactions.feedback: Well done! Have, has and me fit correctly.
interactions.retryHint: Use has with she; use have with they.

interactions.prompt: Akinyi is my sister. I sit beside ___.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the objective pronoun for a girl or woman.

interactions.prompt: Juma has a kite. I help ___ fly ___.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Him replaces Juma and it replaces the kite.
interactions.retryHint: The first blank is a boy; the second is a thing.

choices: She has a bag. Give it to her.
She have a bag. Give him to it.
She has a bag. Give me to him.
interactions.answer: She has a bag. Give it to her.
interactions.feedback: Super! You used has, it and her correctly.
interactions.retryHint: Use has with she; it for the bag; her for the girl.
